description: Admin-only rider payment-history + refunds endpoint. New additive route GET /payments/admin/rider/<rider_id>/payments/ returning this rider's Payment rows ONLY (data isolation), server-side paginated with optional ?status=, plus a `refunds` key of the rider's RefundRequest rows. NEVER expose provider_token or full card data. Independent of FEAT-001 and FEAT-003. Grounded in: payments/models.py — Payment(rider FK, ride_id, amount, currency default MRU, method, status, transaction_id, created_at; NO provider_token, NO resolved_at); RefundRequest(FK customer, FK payment_record, amount, reason, status, created_at, resolved_at; currency only via payment_record.currency); PaymentRecord HAS provider_token (never expose).
steps: Create backend/taxi/payments/admin_rider_serializers.py with two NEW serializers (do NOT modify existing payments serializers). AdminRiderPaymentSerializer(ModelSerializer on Payment): fields = transaction_id, ride_id, amount, currency, method, status, created_at — and explicitly NOTHING else (no provider_token — Payment has none anyway, no card fields). AdminRiderRefundSerializer(ModelSerializer on RefundRequest): id, amount, currency (SerializerMethodField returning obj.payment_record.currency if obj.payment_record else 'MRU'), reason, status, created_at, resolved_at.

In backend/taxi/payments/wallet_views.py add a PageNumberPagination subclass (page_size=25, page_size_query_param='page_size', max_page_size=100) OR reuse one if an equivalent already exists in the module.

In backend/taxi/payments/wallet_views.py add view admin_rider_payments(request, rider_id) decorated @api_view(['GET']) + @permission_classes([IsAdminUser]). Resolve the rider via get_object_or_404(User, id=rider_id) with the same not-a-rider -> 404 rule as FEAT-001 (reuse an identical helper or inline comment). Build qs = Payment.objects.filter(rider_id=rider_id).order_by('-created_at'); optional ?status= filter; same malformed-date-handling policy if date filters are added (optional for payments — if you add ?date_from/?date_to, malformed -> 400 to stay consistent).

Paginate the payment rows with the pagination class. Attach refunds = AdminRiderRefundSerializer(RefundRequest.objects.filter(customer_id=rider_id).select_related('payment_record').order_by('-created_at'), many=True).data under a top-level `refunds` key alongside the paginated payments.
Register the route in backend/taxi/payments/urls.py: path('admin/rider/<int:rider_id>/payments/', admin_rider_payments) and import the view from .wallet_views.

Add tests in backend/taxi/tests/payments/test_admin_rider_payments.py following tests/operations/test_admin_permissions.py. Cover: anonymous -> 401/403; non-staff rider -> 403; admin -> 200; a DIFFERENT rider's payments/refunds are never returned; pagination cap enforced; optional ?status= filter; refunds for the rider appear under `refunds`; and ASSERT that provider_token and any full-card/PAN field are absent from the serialized payload (serialize a Payment and confirm the response keys are exactly the allowed set).
acceptance_criteria: GET /payments/admin/rider/<rider_id>/payments/ exists, is IsAdminUser-gated, returns only Payment rows where rider_id == rider_id, server-side paginated (default 25, cap 100), with optional ?status=.
Response includes a `refunds` key containing only RefundRequest rows for customer_id == rider_id, with currency derived from the related PaymentRecord.
Serialized payload NEVER contains provider_token or full card data; payment fields are limited to transaction_id, ride_id, amount, currency, method, status, created_at.
No existing endpoint, serializer, or route is modified; no migration is added.
Running `<venv-python> manage.py test tests.payments.test_admin_rider_payments` passes all new tests.
findings:
IMPLEMENTED. Route: GET /payments/admin/rider/<int:rider_id>/payments/ (registered in backend/taxi/payments/urls.py, view imported from .wallet_views), IsAdminUser-gated.

RESPONSE ENVELOPE (reuses FEAT-001's custom top-level shape for frontend consistency, with `refunds` replacing `summary`):
{
  "count": <int total matching Payment rows across pages>,
  "page": <int 1-based current page>,
  "page_size": <int effective page size (<=100)>,
  "total_pages": <int>,
  "results": [ <AdminRiderPaymentSerializer rows> ],
  "refunds": [ <AdminRiderRefundSerializer rows, rider's full refund history> ]
}

PAGINATION: AdminRiderPaymentsPagination(PageNumberPagination) page_size=25, page_size_query_param='page_size', max_page_size=100 (added in wallet_views.py).

FILTER: optional ?status= validated against Payment.PAYMENT_STATUS_CHOICES; unknown value silently ignored (no filter), consistent with FEAT-001's status handling. No date filters added (optional per spec).

NOT-A-RIDER RULE: identical to FEAT-001 — get_object_or_404(User, id=rider_id), then HTTP 404 if user.is_staff or user.is_superuser or hasattr(user,'driver_profile').

SERIALIZERS (new file backend/taxi/payments/admin_rider_serializers.py; no existing serializer modified):
- AdminRiderPaymentSerializer(Payment): fields exactly [transaction_id, ride_id, amount, currency, method, status, created_at]. Payment has no provider_token/card fields; nothing sensitive can leak.
- AdminRiderRefundSerializer(RefundRequest): fields [id, amount, currency, reason, status, created_at, resolved_at]; currency is a SerializerMethodField returning obj.payment_record.currency (or 'MRU' when missing). The related PaymentRecord — which DOES carry provider_token — is never serialized. qs uses .select_related('payment_record') for the currency lookup only.

DATA ISOLATION: Payment.objects.filter(rider_id=rider_id); RefundRequest.objects.filter(customer_id=rider_id). A different rider's payments/refunds never appear (asserted).

SENSITIVE-FIELD GUARANTEE: test asserts payment row keys == the 7 allowed fields exactly, and that the full response body contains neither 'provider_token' nor a seeded secret token value.

TESTS: backend/taxi/tests/payments/test_admin_rider_payments.py (11 tests, all pass). Also added backend/taxi/tests/payments/__init__.py (the tests/payments/ package did not exist yet; without the __init__.py the `tests.payments` label fails Django test discovery with a TypeError). Verification: `manage.py test tests.payments.test_admin_rider_payments` = 11 OK; `manage.py test tests.payments` = 32 OK (11 new + 21 pre-existing, no regressions).

PRE-EXISTING DRIFT NOTE (NOT fixed — out of additive scope): the RefundRequest model class in payments/models.py is out of sync with migration 0021_sprint6_finance_driver_ops (model does NOT declare requires_dual_approval / finance_approved_at / finance_approved_by, nor the 'awaiting_ceo' status choice, all of which the migration added). Because the ORM is unaware of requires_dual_approval (NOT NULL, no DB default), a plain RefundRequest.objects.create(...) raises IntegrityError: NOT NULL constraint failed: payments_refundrequest.requires_dual_approval. The same latent bug affects payments/settlement_service.request_refund. To avoid touching existing models/migrations, the test seeds RefundRequest rows via a raw INSERT (_create_refund helper) against the real schema. This drift should be flagged to the owner for a follow-up model/migration reconciliation; it does NOT affect the read-only endpoint (filter/serialize of existing rows works fine).

Additive only: no existing endpoint/serializer/route/auth/media changed; no model changes or migrations. provider_token / full card data are never exposed.
